annotation_description: Chose to be on the draw in Standard constructed, giving up the tempo advantage of going first. In nearly all Standard constructed matchups, being on the play is preferred as it provides a tempo advantage in mana development and threat deployment.

Cast Seam Rip on turn 1 when the opponent has no nonland permanents on the battlefield. Seam Rip's ETB trigger requires targeting a nonland permanent an opponent controls with mana value 2 or less, but there are none. The enchantment enters but its ability fizzles, wasting the card entirely. Seam Rip would have been very useful later to exile a small creature or enchantment the opponent plays.

Rest in Peace is a graveyard hate card being deployed on turn 2 with no evidence the opponent is running graveyard synergies. The opponent's visible cards (Fountainport, Seam Rip) don't suggest a graveyard-dependent strategy. While it's not a wasted card (it's a permanent that could matter later), spending the turn on speculative hate rather than holding up interaction or developing more impactfully seems suboptimal.

Using Get Lost on Enduring Innocence when Day of Judgment is in hand for next turn and Rest in Peace ensures Enduring Innocence won't return when destroyed. Get Lost gives the opponent 2 Map tokens unnecessarily. Additionally, Seam Rip could have been used to remove the opponent's Seam Rip to recover the exiled permanent, while saving Get Lost for a harder-to-answer threat like Ajani.

message: Select a creature, enchantment, or planeswalker
annotation_description: GPT5n used Get Lost to destroy the opponent's Seam Rip instead of Enduring Innocence. Seam Rip is exiling one of GPT5n's permanents (likely a small creature or permanent), but Enduring Innocence is a much more dangerous threat - it's a 2/1 lifelink creature that draws cards whenever small creatures enter, and it returns as an enchantment when it dies (though Rest in Peace would exile it instead). With Rest in Peace in play, Get Lost on Enduring Innocence would permanently remove it since it would be exiled instead of returning. Meanwhile, destroying Seam Rip gives the opponent two Map tokens and only recovers whatever was exiled. Enduring Innocence is the key card advantage engine that will generate significant value over the course of the game, especially since the opponent has token generation (Fountainport, and potentially Ajani). Additionally, GPT5n has Day of Judgment in hand which could handle creatures later, but removing the card advantage engine now while Rest in Peace ensures it stays dead is the stronger line.

Opponent has no creatures on the battlefield. Quantum Riddler (4/6 flying) could attack for free alongside Enduring Innocence, dealing 6 total damage instead of just 2. There is no reason to hold back the Riddler when there are no blockers and no combat tricks to worry about.

chosen_display: 2. {T}: Add {U}. Activate only if you control a Plains or an Island.
annotation_description: Tapped Floodfarm Verge for {U} when their hand contains only white spells (Ajani, Seam Rip, High Noon). Blue mana is useless here - they need white mana to cast any of their spells.

High Noon limits each player to one spell per turn. GLM47 Snark has Enduring Curiosity (a powerful 4/3 flash creature with card draw) and Ajani in hand, plus Enduring Innocence on board that draws cards when small creatures enter. High Noon symmetrically locks both players to one spell per turn, but GLM47 has a hand full of impactful spells (Enduring Curiosity, Ajani, Seam Rip) that they'll now be unable to deploy quickly. The opponent has an empty board except for enchantments (two Seam Rips exiling something), so they're not casting many spells anyway. Playing Ajani instead would create tokens (triggering Enduring Innocence for card draw) and apply pressure, which seems more impactful than a symmetrical lock that hurts GLM47's own development more than the opponent's current position.

With High Noon limiting each player to one spell per turn, casting Consult the Star Charts instead of Day of Judgment wastes a turn while Enduring Innocence continues attacking with lifelink. Importantly, Rest in Peace (which Rivals controls) would exile Enduring Innocence when it dies, preventing its return-to-battlefield trigger, making Day of Judgment a permanent answer to the creature.

GPT5n Rivals is at 14 life facing an Enduring Innocence (2/1 lifelink) and High Noon on board, with the opponent at 26 life and building advantage. Day of Judgment would destroy Enduring Innocence, which would return as an enchantment (losing its creature status and lifelink/combat ability). While High Noon limits casting to one spell per turn, this was the postcombat main phase and Day of Judgment was available as a choice. Instead, GPT5n activated Cori Mountain Monastery's ability (spending 4 mana to exile the top card for future use), which is far less impactful. The Enduring Innocence is gaining life and triggering card draw for the opponent, and removing it as a creature is important. Casting Day of Judgment now would stop the bleeding, and under High Noon they can only cast one spell per turn anyway, so delaying means another turn of attacks and lifegain.

With High Noon restricting each player to one spell per turn, casting Consult the Star Charts wastes the turn's spell on card selection instead of impacting the board. Rivals is at 14 life facing Enduring Innocence (lifelink) and Restless Anchorage, and has Day of Judgment or The Unagi of Kyoshi Island available as much more impactful plays.

GPT5n Rivals is at 12 life facing an opponent with High Noon on the battlefield, which restricts each player to one spell per turn. By casting The Unagi of Kyoshi Island (a 5/5 creature) as their one spell this turn, they cannot cast Day of Judgment this turn. The opponent has Enduring Innocence attacking with lifelink, and GPT5n is at 12 life and falling behind. Day of Judgment is urgently needed to clear the board and stabilize. Furthermore, casting a 5/5 creature into a board where the opponent can untap and use Ajani's -2 to deal 4 damage to a tapped creature, or where the opponent has Seam Rip-style answers, is risky. Most critically, High Noon means they're locked out of casting Day of Judgment this turn, and by next turn they may be even further behind or dead. The Unagi doesn't block effectively against the current threats when what's needed is a board wipe.

GPT5n Rivals is casting The Unagi of Kyoshi Island (a 5/5 creature for 3UU) during their precombat main phase while High Noon is on the battlefield, which limits each player to one spell per turn. The opponent has Enduring Innocence attacking and the Rivals player is at 12 life. They have Day of Judgment in hand which would clear the board of the opponent's Enduring Innocence (and any other creatures). By casting The Unagi instead of Day of Judgment, they use their one spell for the turn on a creature that doesn't immediately address the board pressure, while the opponent's High Noon prevents them from also casting Day of Judgment this turn. Furthermore, the opponent is at 28 life with an established board including Restless Anchorage (which can become a creature), so the Unagi alone won't race effectively. Day of Judgment would reset the board and stop the bleeding, which is critical at 12 life. The Unagi can potentially be cast later (it has flash), whereas clearing the board is more urgent.

message: Select a creature, enchantment, or planeswalker
annotation_description: High Noon restricts GPT5n Rivals to one spell per turn, which is devastating when they're at 10 life vs 30 life with a hand full of powerful spells (Day of Judgment, Jeskai Revelation, multiple card draw). Additionally, Enduring Curiosity has the Glimmer ability - when destroyed as a creature, it returns as an enchantment and retains its combat damage card-draw ability, so Get Lost doesn't even permanently remove it.

Opponent is at 10 life with no flyers to block. Restless Anchorage could be animated as a 2/3 flyer for 2 extra damage plus a Map token, applying significant pressure. The mana was available to activate it.

At 1 life facing lethal attacks from Enduring Innocence, activating Cori Mountain Monastery's expensive ability (costing 4 mana + tap) leaves only 2 untapped lands, making it impossible to cast the critical Day of Judgment ({2}{W}{W}) this turn. The opponent can simply attack for lethal next combat.

At 1 life with 3 lands already in hand (2x Sunbillow Verge + Island), picking another land over a second Jeskai Revelation is suboptimal. Jeskai Revelation provides crucial life gain (4 life), removal, card draw, and board presence - all critical when at 1 life.
